description.narrative: The project will assist the Government of Assam in strengthening its skills education and training system to ensure decent employment for all and accelerate sustainable and inclusive infrastructure and industrial development. It will create pathways for skills progression and mobility between technical and vocational education and training (TVET) and higher education through the establishment of a skill university, and will raise skill levels to enhance the productivity and competitiveness of industries in Assam. The project will enhance skills and employability of youth and adults, especially women and those from disadvantaged groups, and improve their prospect of getting higher-paying, decent jobs. The project will form part of the strategic engagement of the Asian Development Bank (ADB) with the Government of Assam for economic corridor development, environmental sustainability, and climate change.

Output: Access to professional development and quality skills education and training resources in Assam, other states, and neighboring countries improved. Indicator: At least 400 trainers, instructors, and assessors of ITIs and polytechnics (40% of all female trainers, instructors, and assessors of ITIs and polytechnics in Assam) completed professional development programs offered at ASU by 2026 Progress/Status: 5b. Deliverable 10a (Training needs assessments of trainers, instructors, assessors, and faculty members of ITIs, polytechnics, and engineering colleges of Assam and the Northeastern region) submitted to ASU on 16th Aug 2025. Deliverable was presented in 10th EC meeting on 20th Feb 2026 and was approved. 10a presents the findings from TNA exercise conducted with instructors and faculty members of different ITIs, polytechnics and engineering colleges of Assam. Major recommendations include targeted training across key areas such as digital proficiency (ICT), collaborative networking, problem-solving and critical thinking, regulatory frameworks and compliance, domain/department-specific training, and exposure to current industry practices. Deliverable has been presented to and approved by CS03 Review Committee.
Key activities carried out by ASU with regards to “FDPs for faculty including ITI / Polytechnic faculty” are as follows: • Advancing Careers Through Technology, Management, and Skill Based Learning - 3rd to 7th March 2025 (25 Participants). • FDP on Advanced Computing with MATLAB, SOLIDWORKS & Python (36 Participants). • FDP for new ASU Faculties conducted at the ASU Interim campus on 9th June to 13th June 2025. • FDP by HAMK, Finland for ASU Faculties was conducted at Guwahati from 15th to 26th September.

Output: Environmentally sustainable and climate resilient university campus and facilities developed. Indicator: ASU campus, academic and administration buildings, faculty and student residential buildings, and other buildings and facilities designed and constructed meeting green building standards and with measures for energy and water saving, climate adaptation, and addressing the needs of females, people with disabilities, and other disadvantaged groups by 2026 Progress/Status: The overall physical progress of campus is 86%.
- Compliances with respect to Green Building are ongoing. Further, the IT-03 firm for Building Management System (BMS) has been onboarded on 28/08/2025. - With respect to addressing the needs of women, people with disabilities, and other disadvantaged groups, it is to be stated that the Entire campus is designed for barrier free access. The design contractor has assessed the designs of all the buildings of the ASU main campus. A detailed checklist has been prepared to address needs of women and people with disabilities. The design of the ASU main campus is as follows - i. Entire campus is designed for barrier free access. ii. All buildings have access ramps and lifts to access all spaces. iii. All the public buildings have barrier-free toilets which can be used by differently abled people, including all men, women, and special persons. iv. Signages will be provided for information on barrier-free features. v. Girls and boys' hostels have designated special rooms with barrier free toilets with shower area. vi. Barrier free parking is provided for all the buildings. vii. Railing is provided for all the steps and staircases. viii. Pathway has tactile flooring. ix. Public address system (announcements) is provided for emergencies. x. The layout with respect to location of blocks are final. The level of roads and area around the blocks are still under discussion. xi. ASU has been registered for Indian Green Building Council (IGBC) rating with following targets: a. IGBC green building rating for administrative and academic buildings. b. ASU campus is targeting for gold standard rating from IGBC.
Data Source: Detailed design and drawings of ASU campus and facilities; construction supervision monitoring and acceptance reports Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: Not Applicable Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: Not Applicable Target year: 2026 Target value: Y
